# Thomas Fence

> Thomas Fence (Paschal Enterprises, Inc.) is a licensed fence contractor serving Northwest Arkansas since 1993. Owner Greg Paschal has operated the business since 2003. Licensed, insured, and certified: Arkansas Contractor License No. 0155010427, AFA Certified Fence Contractor, CGAT Certified Gate Automation Technician, US Federal Contractor Registration. Located at 653 Kawneer Dr, Springdale, AR 72764. Phone: (479) 636-4732. Hours: Mon–Fri, 8am–4pm.

### About Thomas Fence | Family-Owned in Springdale Since 1993 (https://thomasfencear.com/about-us/)

**Q: Who is Thomas Fence?**
A: Thomas Fence is a Northwest Arkansas fence and gate company founded in 1993 and owned by Greg Paschal since 2003. We build residential, commercial, and farm fencing along with automated gates, from our home base in Springdale.

**Q: Is Thomas Fence licensed and certified?**
A: Yes — Arkansas Contractor's License No. 0155010427, held since 2005 and renewed annually. Thomas Fence is also an AFA Certified Fence Contractor with a Certified Gate Automation Technician on staff. See our licensing and credentials page for the full list.

**Q: Where is Thomas Fence located, and what areas do you serve?**
A: Our office and yard are at 653 Kawneer Dr, Springdale, AR 72764, and we serve all of Northwest Arkansas — see the full service area.

**Q: What kinds of projects does Thomas Fence take on?**
A: Everything from backyard privacy fences to commercial and farm fencing, plus gates and railings including automated gate systems. Browse our fencing services to see the full range.

**Q: How do I get an estimate?**
A: Request a free estimate and we will walk your property line with you, or get an instant number from the fence estimator.

### Fence Company in Bella Vista, AR | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/bella-vista/)

**Q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Bella Vista?**
A: Yes — two approvals: a city permit and ACC (Architectural Control Committee) approval, both before installation. Start with the city permit portal and the ACC permits page.

**Q: How tall can my fence be in Bella Vista?**
A: Up to 8 feet in side and back yards, 3 feet in front yards, and chain link tops out at 6 feet. The ACC confirms what applies to your lot.

**Q: Does the ACC restrict fence types?**
A: Yes — no chain link or wire in front yards, and no white fencing has been permitted since 2022. Check with the ACC before choosing a style, or call them at (479) 855-8080.

**Q: Who calls for the utility locate?**
A: Thomas Fence does — Arkansas law requires an Arkansas 811 utility locate before digging, and it takes 2 full business days. We call it in for every project.

**Q: How soon can my fence be installed?**
A: Work typically starts 1–3 weeks after you accept your estimate, and most residential fences take 2–3 business days to install.

**Q: How do I get an estimate in Bella Vista?**
A: Estimates are free. Request yours or get an instant number from the fence estimator.

**Q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Bentonville?**

**Q: How tall can my fence be in Bentonville?**
A: In typical residential zones: 4 feet in the front and 6 feet for privacy fences on the sides and back. Confirm your zone with the city.

**Q: How close to the street or property line can I build?**
A: Fences must stay at least 5 feet from the right-of-way, keep sight triangles clear, and stay out of drainage easements. The city's applications page has the details.

### Fence Installation FAQs | Thomas Fence | Northwest Arkansas (https://thomasfencear.com/faqs/)

**Q: Does Thomas Fence have an Arkansas Contractor's License?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence holds Arkansas Contractor's License No. 0155010427, maintained continuously since 2005 and renewed annually. You can verify our license status at any time through the Arkansas Contractor's Licensing Board. See thomasfencear.com/licensing/ for our full credentials.

**Q: Is Thomas Fence AFA Certified?**
A: Yes. Through the American Fence Association and the Accredited Contractor Institute (ACI), Thomas Fence became Arkansas's first Certified Fence Contractor. This accreditation is awarded after proving excellence in business practices, passing industry-specific testing, and maintaining a trusted professional reputation. It is renewed every three years through advanced training.

**Q: Is Thomas Fence a Certified Gate Automation Technician (CGAT)?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence holds the CGAT designation — the premier certification for automated gate installers. Our technicians have demonstrated exceptional experience, knowledge, safety awareness, and skills in the installation and servicing of automated gate systems.

**Q: Is Thomas Fence a US Federal Contractor?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence is a verified US Federal Contractor Registration (USFCR) vendor, authorized to perform fencing contracts for government facilities, military installations, and large-scale public projects.

**Q: Is Thomas Fence bonded and insured?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence is fully bonded and insured. Every project is covered from the first post to the final inspection. Proof of insurance is available upon request.

**Q: Is a fence permit required for my fence in Northwest Arkansas?**
A: Not in every city. Seven Northwest Arkansas cities require a fence permit: Bella Vista, Bentonville, Gravette, Gentry, Lincoln, Prairie Grove and Tontitown. Springdale, Rogers, Fayetteville and Siloam Springs do not. HOA rules apply separately and requirements can change, so verify with your city before starting. Thomas Fence keeps a current list with links to each town's permitting site at thomasfencear.com/permits/. Each customer is responsible for obtaining their own permit.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence pull permits for customers?**
A: No. Because rules vary significantly between cities and HOAs, each customer handles their own permit. Thomas Fence is happy to assist and answer questions about the process.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence stain fences?**
A: No. Fence staining requires a different skill set. Thomas Fence refers customers to trusted local staining companies.

**Q: How long before Thomas Fence can start after I accept a quote?**
A: Typically 1 to 3 weeks from acceptance. There is always a 2-full-business-day window to complete the required underground utility locate. A project manager will call 1 to 2 days before crews arrive.

**Q: Who calls One Call to get utilities located?**
A: Thomas Fence. State law requires the person or company performing the work to call in the locate. Customers do not need to do this.

**Q: How long does a utility locate take?**
A: By law, utility companies have 2 full business days to locate and mark underground lines after the 811 request is submitted. This is a fixed requirement, not an estimate. Note that they only mark lines they own. Privately owned lines such as septic, irrigation, outbuilding electric, and pool gas are not marked.

**Q: What underground utilities are not marked in a One Call locate?**
A: Privately owned lines downstream from a meter are not marked. Examples include septic lines, electric lines to outbuildings, gas lines to outdoor grills or pool equipment, irrigation lines, and water lines from wells.

**Q: How long does fence installation take?**
A: A typical residential fence installation takes 2 to 3 business days, depending on the type and length of fence.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence use concrete for fence posts?**
A: Yes. As a best practice, posts are set in concrete unless otherwise agreed upon with the customer.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence require a deposit?**
A: No deposit is required for standard installations. The exception is special order materials or custom metal work. Thomas Fence prefers to wait until the job is completed before requesting payment.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence offer a veteran's discount?**
A: No, Thomas Fence does not currently offer a veteran's discount.

**Q: Is there a discount for paying with cash?**
A: No, Thomas Fence is not able to offer a discount for cash payments.

**Q: Can I pay with a credit card?**
A: Yes. A 3.5% processing fee is added to the invoice when a credit card is used to cover the processing fee charged by the credit card company.

**Q: What warranty does Thomas Fence offer?**
A: Thomas Fence offers a one-year craftsmanship warranty included in every written contract.

**Q: How long should I wait before staining a new wood fence?**
A: It depends on the wood type and season. Pressure-treated pine typically needs 1 to 3 months to dry before staining. Cedar can usually be stained immediately.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence offer financing?**
A: Yes. Financing is available through Hearth, a third-party lender serving the fencing industry. Apply by scanning the QR code on your estimate or visit thomasfencear.com/financing/.

### Fence Company in Fayetteville, AR | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/fayetteville/)

**Q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Fayetteville?**
A: Not for most fences — 7 feet tall or less needs no permit, per the city's permit FAQ. Taller than 7 feet requires a building permit through Building Safety.

**Q: How tall can my fence be in Fayetteville?**
A: Behind the house there is no set cap — 7 feet is just where a permit kicks in. In front of the house, a fence can be solid only up to 30 inches. Details: Building Safety.

**Q: How close to the street or property line can I build?**
A: Fences can sit on the property line, but nothing over 30 inches can block sight lines, and corner lots keep a 25-foot sight triangle clear at the intersection. Ask the city about your lot: Building Safety.

**Q: Who calls for the utility locate?**
A: Thomas Fence does — Arkansas law requires an Arkansas 811 utility locate before digging, and it takes 2 full business days. We call it in for every project.

**Q: How soon can my fence be installed?**
A: Work typically starts 1–3 weeks after you accept your estimate, and most residential fences take 2–3 business days to install.

**Q: How do I get an estimate in Fayetteville?**
A: Estimates are free. Request yours or get an instant number from the fence estimator.

### Chain Link Fences in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/fences/chain-link-fence/)

**Q: Do I need a permit to install a chain link fence in Arkansas?**
A: Not in every city. Seven Northwest Arkansas cities require a fence permit: Bella Vista, Bentonville, Gravette, Gentry, Lincoln, Prairie Grove and Tontitown. Springdale, Rogers, Fayetteville and Siloam Springs do not. Requirements can change, so verify with your city before starting. Pulling the permit is the homeowner's or property owner's responsibility, and Thomas Fence is happy to walk you through the process. See the Fence Permits page at thomasfencear.com/permits/ for links to each town's permit office.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence pull permits?**
A: No — permits are the customer's responsibility. However, our team is happy to answer questions and help guide you through the process so nothing gets missed before installation begins.

**Q: How long does it take to install a chain link fence?**
A: Most residential chain link fence installations take 2 to 3 business days. Larger commercial or industrial projects may take longer. Once the contract is signed, we typically schedule your project within 1 to 3 weeks.

**Q: What gauges of chain link do you install?**
A: We install a full range of chain link gauges depending on your application. Standard residential installations typically use 11-gauge or 11.5-gauge fabric. Commercial and industrial applications call for heavier 9-gauge fabric and larger posts. Our estimators will recommend the right spec for your project.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence use concrete for chain link posts?**
A: Yes. All posts are set in concrete as standard practice, unless otherwise agreed upon in the contract. Concrete footings ensure long-term stability and are especially important in Arkansas's clay-heavy soils.

**Q: Is a deposit required for a chain link fence installation?**
A: No deposit is required for standard chain link fence installations. A deposit may be required for special-order materials or custom fabrication. Your estimator will confirm terms when reviewing your project.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence offer financing for chain link fence projects?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence offers financing through Hearth with loan amounts up to $250,000. Apply online or ask your sales representative for a QR code. Checking your rate does not impact your credit score. See our Financing page for details.

**Q: What is the difference between galvanized and vinyl-coated chain link?**
A: Galvanized chain link has a zinc coating that resists rust — it is the standard, cost-effective option for most applications. Vinyl-coated chain link adds a PVC layer in black, green, or other colors for a finished appearance and added corrosion resistance. Both are durable; vinyl-coated is more common where appearance matters or in coastal or high-moisture environments.

**Q: Can chain link fence be made private?**
A: Yes. Privacy slats can be woven through the chain link fabric to block sightlines. This is a cost-effective alternative to a full privacy fence. Slats are available in several colors and can be added at installation or retrofitted to an existing chain link fence.

**Q: Is chain link fence appropriate for commercial properties?**
A: Yes — chain link is one of the most common choices for commercial and industrial perimeters because of its durability, low maintenance, and cost-effectiveness. Thomas Fence installs commercial-grade chain link for warehouses, distribution centers, schools, and government facilities across Northwest Arkansas.

### Farm Fence Installation in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/fences/farm-fencing/)

**Q: How long before my farm fence project can start?**
A: Once you sign the contract, Thomas Fence typically starts your project within 1–3 weeks. We call 811 before any digging — state law requires a 2-full-business-day utility locate window before post setting can begin. For large rural properties, the total installation timeline depends on linear footage and site conditions.

**Q: What's the best fence for horses?**
A: Horses need a fence that provides a clear visual barrier without injury risk. Non-climb woven wire with a top board or rail is the most common solution — horses can see it clearly and won't get legs caught in the mesh. Board fencing (2- or 3-rail) is excellent for smaller paddocks and arenas. We recommend against barbed wire for horse enclosures due to injury risk.

**Q: Can you fence a large rural property?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence handles agricultural fencing projects of all sizes across Northwest Arkansas — from small backyard animal runs to large multi-acre ranch perimeters. We provide detailed estimates based on linear footage and terrain, and our crews are equipped for large-scale rural work.

**Q: Is a deposit required for farm fencing?**
A: No deposit is required for standard farm fence installations. The exception is special-order materials. Thomas Fence prefers to wait until the work is completed before requesting payment.

**Q: What types of farm fencing does Thomas Fence install?**
A: Thomas Fence installs woven wire, high-tensile wire, board fencing, T-post, and barbed wire fencing for agricultural properties across Northwest Arkansas. We also install Buckley Fence polymer rail systems — a popular choice for horse properties and livestock operations.

**Q: What is Buckley Fence and why does Thomas Fence recommend it?**
A: Buckley Fence is a high-strength polymer rail system commonly used for horse properties and livestock fencing. The rail material is impact-resistant and will not splinter like wood, reducing injury risk for animals. Thomas Fence is an authorized Buckley Fence dealer and installer in Northwest Arkansas.

**Q: Can wire mesh be added to Buckley rail fencing?**
A: Yes. Wire mesh can be added behind Buckley rails to contain smaller animals or provide additional security. This is a popular configuration for properties with horses and smaller livestock. Your estimator can show you the available mesh options during your consultation.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence install agricultural gates?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence installs farm gates in pipe, tube, and panel styles. Gate automation is also available for agricultural applications. Contact us to discuss your layout and livestock management requirements.

**Q: Is a permit required for farm fencing in Arkansas?**
A: Permit requirements for agricultural fencing vary by county and zoning classification. Rural fencing is often exempt from standard residential permit requirements. Thomas Fence will advise you on local requirements for your specific location during the estimate process.

### Fencing Services in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/fences/)

**Q: What types of fences does Thomas Fence install?**
A: Thomas Fence installs vinyl, wood, chain link, and ornamental steel fencing, along with residential, commercial, farm, and temporary fence projects across Northwest Arkansas — and we have been doing it since 1993.

**Q: How much does a new fence cost in Northwest Arkansas?**
A: Every project is different — cost depends on the material, the length of the fence line, gates, and the terrain. The fastest way to get a number is the instant fence estimator on thomasfencear.com, or contact Thomas Fence for a free on-site estimate. There is no deposit required except for special orders or custom metal work.

**Q: How soon can my fence be installed?**
A: Work typically begins 1–3 weeks after you accept your estimate. Before digging, Arkansas law requires a utility locate through Arkansas 811, which takes 2 full business days — Thomas Fence calls that in for you. A typical residential installation then takes 2–3 business days.

**Q: Do I need a permit, and who pulls it?**
A: Not every city. Seven Northwest Arkansas cities require a fence permit: Bella Vista, Bentonville, Gravette, Gentry, Lincoln, Prairie Grove and Tontitown. Springdale, Rogers, Fayetteville and Siloam Springs do not. Requirements can change, so verify with your city before starting. Pulling the permit is the property owner's responsibility, and Thomas Fence is happy to help you understand your city's process, with links to each town's permit office on the Fence Permits page.

**Q: Which fence material is right for my property?**
A: It depends on what the fence needs to do. Vinyl offers privacy with almost no maintenance, wood is the classic look for backyards, chain link is the best value for security and pets, and ornamental steel adds curb appeal that lasts for decades. The Thomas Fence team will walk your property line and help you choose during your free estimate.

**Q: Are the fence posts set in concrete?**

### Vinyl Fence Contractor in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/fences/vinyl-fence/)

**Q: Do I need a permit to install a vinyl fence in Arkansas?**

See the Fence Permits page at thomasfencear.com/permits/ for links to each town's permit office.

**Q: Does vinyl fence require maintenance?**
A: Vinyl fencing is essentially maintenance-free. It does not need to be painted, stained, or treated for rot. An occasional rinse with a garden hose or light pressure wash is all that's needed to keep vinyl looking clean and new — one of the biggest advantages vinyl has over wood.

**Q: How does vinyl hold up in Northwest Arkansas weather?**
A: Vinyl fencing holds up well in NWA's climate. It won't warp, crack, or absorb moisture the way wood can. Quality vinyl is UV-stabilized to resist fading in the Arkansas sun. It is not immune to impact damage, but for normal residential use it performs reliably for many years.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence use concrete for vinyl fence posts?**
A: Yes. All posts are set in concrete as standard practice, unless otherwise agreed upon in the contract. Concrete footings are especially important for vinyl fencing because the material relies on a solid post foundation to stay plumb and resist wind load over time.

**Q: How long does it take to install a vinyl fence?**
A: Most residential vinyl fence installations take 2 to 3 business days. Once the contract is signed, we typically schedule your project within 1 to 3 weeks. A 2-full-business-day utility locate window is required by state law before any digging begins.

**Q: Will vinyl fence warp or fade in Arkansas summers?**
A: Professional-grade vinyl fence is engineered to resist heat, UV exposure, warping, and fading. Thomas Fence installs commercial-quality vinyl products — not the lower-grade materials found at big-box stores. Properly installed vinyl fence maintains its color and shape for decades in Northwest Arkansas's climate.

**Q: What warranty does vinyl fence carry?**

### Wood Fence Contractor in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/fences/wood-fence/)

**Q: Do I need a permit to install a wood fence in Arkansas?**
A: Not in every city. Seven Northwest Arkansas cities require a fence permit: Bella Vista, Bentonville, Gravette, Gentry, Lincoln, Prairie Grove and Tontitown. Springdale, Rogers, Fayetteville and Siloam Springs do not. Requirements can change, so verify with your city before starting. Pulling the permit is the homeowner's or property owner's responsibility, and Thomas Fence is happy to walk you through the process. See the Fence Permits page at thomasfencear.com/permits/ for links to each town's permit office.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence stain wood fences?**
A: No — Thomas Fence does not stain fences. We are happy to refer you to local staining companies after installation. If you're planning to stain, keep in mind: cedar can be stained immediately after installation, while pressure-treated pine should wait 1 to 3 months to allow moisture to escape before staining.

**Q: What wood species does Thomas Fence use?**
A: Thomas Fence primarily builds with cedar and pressure-treated pine. Cedar is naturally rot-resistant and a premium choice for privacy and decorative fences. Pressure-treated pine is a durable, cost-effective option for most residential applications. Your estimator will discuss the best fit for your project and budget.

**Q: What species of cedar does Thomas Fence use?**
A: Western red cedar almost exclusively. Thomas Fence will occasionally run Japanese cedar for a builder or a residential customer, but it is rare, and it does not build with eastern red cedar. Western red and Japanese cedar both get sold as cedar and they price very differently, so ask anyone bidding your fence which one is on the estimate. Western red is the higher quality material. Measured on price, Japanese cedar is the better number and a real step up from treated pine, so it is a legitimate choice and not a lesser one. The full comparison is at thomasfencear.com/publications/what-species-of-cedar-is-your-fence-western-red-japanese-and-eastern-red-cedar-in-northwest-arkansas/.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence use concrete for wood fence posts?**
A: Yes. All posts are set in concrete as standard practice, unless otherwise agreed upon in the contract. Concrete footings ensure long-term stability, which is especially important in Northwest Arkansas's clay-heavy soils.

**Q: How long does it take to install a wood fence?**
A: Most residential wood fence installations take 2 to 3 business days. Once the contract is signed, we typically schedule your project within 1 to 3 weeks. A 2-full-business-day utility locate window is required by state law before any digging begins.

**Q: Is a deposit required for a wood fence installation?**
A: No deposit is required for standard wood fence installations. A deposit may be required for special-order materials or custom work. Your estimator will confirm payment terms when reviewing your project.

**Q: Does Thomas Fence offer financing for wood fence projects?**
A: Yes. Thomas Fence offers financing through Hearth with loan amounts up to $250,000. Checking your rate does not impact your credit score. See our Financing page for details or ask your sales representative for a QR code to apply.

**Q: How long before I can stain a new wood fence?**
A: For pressure-treated pine, wait 1 to 3 months before staining to allow the wood to fully dry. Cedar can be stained immediately after installation. Thomas Fence does not stain fences, but we are happy to refer you to reputable staining companies in the Northwest Arkansas area.

**Q: What is the difference between cedar and pressure-treated pine?**
A: Cedar is naturally rot-resistant, accepts stain immediately, and has a longer natural lifespan — it is the premium choice. Pressure-treated pine is chemically treated for rot resistance, less expensive, and widely available, but it must dry 1 to 3 months before staining. Both are solid choices; your estimator can help you weigh the trade-offs based on your budget and timeline.

**Q: What warranty does Thomas Fence offer on wood fences?**
A: Thomas Fence provides a 1-year craftsmanship warranty on every installation, included in your written contract. The warranty covers workmanship — post setting, rail attachment, and picket installation. Material warranties depend on the specific wood product.

### Automated Gates in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/gates/automated-gates/)

**Q: Can any gate be automated?**
A: Most gate styles can be automated — swing, slide, cantilever, and others. The key factors are gate weight, opening width, and available power. We assess your site during a consultation to confirm feasibility and recommend the appropriate operator for your specific gate.

**Q: What power source do automated gates need?**
A: Most operators run on standard 120V AC power. For locations where running power to the gate is impractical, solar-powered operators are available — particularly for residential swing gates in sunny climates. We evaluate power options during the site assessment.

**Q: What safety devices are required on an automated gate?**
A: UL 325 requires entrapment protection on all automated gates — typically safety edges, photo eyes, or loop detectors depending on gate type. Thomas Fence installs all required safety devices as part of every gate automation project, not as add-ons.

**Q: Do I need a permit for an automated gate?**
A: Permit requirements vary by municipality. Gates with electrical components are more likely to require a permit than manual gates. Thomas Fence will advise you on local requirements for your specific city — the customer is responsible for obtaining permits, and we are happy to assist with documentation.

**Q: Can you integrate gate automation with a smart home or security system?**
A: Many modern operators support smart home integration via Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, or app-based control. We can discuss compatible systems during your consultation. For advanced security integration, we coordinate with your security provider as needed.

**Q: What does CGAT certification mean?**
A: CGAT stands for Certified Gate Automation Technician — a designation from the American Fence Association (AFA). It requires demonstrated knowledge of gate operator mechanics, UL 325 safety standards, access control systems, and safe installation practices. It is the recognized industry credential for gate automation work.

### Estate Gates in Northwest Arkansas | Thomas Fence (https://thomasfencear.com/gates/estate-gates/)

**Q: What exactly is an estate gate?**
A: An estate gate is a large, custom entrance gate — typically for a driveway or property entrance — designed to make a statement as well as provide security. Estate gates are generally wider and taller than standard gates, built from premium materials, and are often automated.

**Q: Can an estate gate be automated?**
A: Yes — virtually all estate gate styles and materials can be automated. Thomas Fence holds the CGAT certification and installs automated gate systems as part of the same project. We handle the gate, the operator, safety devices, and access control so you work with one contractor from start to finish.

**Q: What material is best for an estate gate?**
A: Ornamental steel is the most popular choice — it offers the best combination of strength, elegance, and longevity with minimal maintenance. Aluminum is lightweight and rust-resistant. Vinyl is low-maintenance with a clean residential look. Chain link is practical for agricultural and commercial applications. We help you weigh the trade-offs during your consultation.

**Q: How wide should a driveway gate be?**
A: For a single-vehicle driveway, 12 feet is generally sufficient. For two-lane driveways or properties with larger vehicles, 16 to 20 feet is common. We measure your driveway during the site visit and recommend an appropriate width based on your vehicles and usage.

**Q: How long does estate gate installation take?**
A: A standard estate gate installation typically takes 1 to 2 days for the gate itself. If automation is added, allow an additional day for the operator, wiring, and access control. Lead time from signed contract to installation start is typically 1 to 3 weeks.

**Q: What is CGAT certification and why does it matter?**
A: The Certified Gate Automation Technician (CGAT) designation is issued by the American Fence Association. It requires demonstrated knowledge of gate operator mechanics, UL 325 safety standards, and access control systems. Automated gates are heavy, fast-moving machines — an improperly installed operator without correct safety devices can cause serious injury. Thomas Fence holds this certification. Most NWA fence contractors do not.

**Q: How long does a gate installation take?**
A: A standard residential gate installation typically takes 1–3 business days. Automated gate systems may take slightly longer depending on access control requirements and concrete curing time for posts. Thomas Fence will give you a timeline estimate before work begins.

Thomas Fence is happy to advise on the permit process — pulling the permit is the property owner's responsibility. See the Fence Permits page at thomasfencear.com/permits/ for links to each town's permit office.

A: Estimates are free. Request yours or get an instant number from the fence estimator. Thomas Fence is headquartered right here in Springdale, at 653 Kawneer Dr.

### Fence Warranty | Thomas Fence | Northwest Arkansas (https://thomasfencear.com/warranty/)

**Q: What warranty does Thomas Fence offer?**
A: Every Thomas Fence installation comes with a 1-year craftsmanship warranty, provided in writing.

**Q: What does the craftsmanship warranty cover?**
A: It covers the quality of our installation work — posts, footings, alignment, gates, and hardware installed by our crew — for one full year.

**Q: Do the fence materials have their own warranties?**
A: Many do. Thomas Fence installs products from reputable manufacturers, and many of those products carry their own manufacturer warranties in addition to our craftsmanship warranty.

**Q: How do I make a warranty claim?**
A: Contact us or call (479) 636-4732 and describe the issue — we will take it from there.
